{
  "id": "p_002",
  "summary": "Design a minimal REST API for task management supporting CRUD operations with standard HTTP methods, JSON data formats, and consistent error handling.",
  "approach": "Define a RESTful API with five endpoints for task management: POST /tasks for creation, GET /tasks for listing, GET /tasks/{id} for retrieval, PUT /tasks/{id} for full updates, and DELETE /tasks/{id} for deletion. Request and response bodies use JSON with a standard task object structure including id (UUID), title, description, status, created_at, and updated_at. Errors return {\"error\": \"message\"}. This design adheres to REST principles, uses HTTP status codes appropriately (e.g., 201 for creation, 204 for deletion), and avoids unnecessary complexity.",
  "tradeoffs": [
    "Using PUT for updates requires sending the full task object, which is less efficient for partial updates but simplifies the API by avoiding PATCH.",
    "No versioning (e.g., /v1/) may cause issues with future API evolution but keeps the design minimal.",
    "No authentication limits security but simplifies implementation and aligns with non-goals.",
    "Focus on core CRUD only, excluding features like pagination or filtering, which may restrict scalability but meets minimal requirements."
  ],
  "evidence": [
    "REST architectural style emphasizes using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) for stateless operations, as defined by Roy Fielding.",
    "JSON is a widely adopted standard for data interchange in REST APIs, supported by most programming languages and tools.",
    "UUIDs for task IDs ensure global uniqueness without coordination, as per RFC 4122.",
    "ISO 8601 timestamps (e.g., '2023-10-01T12:00:00Z') provide a consistent format for created_at and updated_at fields.",
    "Consistent error responses with {\"error\": \"message\"} simplify client-side error handling, a common pattern in APIs like Stripe and GitHub."
  ],
  "artifacts": []
}
